text.tspan: Good thinkers talk to themselves. When a puzzle looks hard, they ask a small question that helps them take
the next step. This ThinkBook gives you
, one for each thinking skill. You will see them
with every question in the book, and you can pick any of them online when you ask Dyna for help. Each one
Connecting a new or difficult idea to something
you already know from daily life
“Can you give a simple example that relates to the core
principles behind the concept this problem is testing?”
A has Rs. 50, B has Rs. 100 and C has Rs. 150. They want to
have equal money. How much do B and C give in all?
It is like three friends sharing sweets so that everyone
gets the same. How many would each friend get?
Deciding how to begin before you start solving
“What step should I take first? Is there an obvious starting
point based on the given information?”
What does this remind me of from my everyday
Where do I begin? Which clue is the easiest to use
Find the largest number name hidden in a row of letters.
Start with the options, not the long row. Write SIXTY,
SIX, TWENTY, SEVENTY and hunt for the biggest first.
